description.value: A 24-month observational study of community-dwelling older adults examining cognitive decline and gray matter density in never smokers, successful quitters, and unsuccessful quitters.

spans.text: We conducted a 3-month non-randomized trial of smoking cessation and a 24-month observational study of community-dwelling older adults living in the metropolitan area of Perth, Australia, between 2003 and 2006.

source_definition.value: Smoking cessation group was a three-level factor comprising never smokers, successful quitters, and unsuccessful quitters. Successful cessation was defined as at least 547 smoking-free days during the 24-month follow-up; unsuccessful cessation was fewer than 547 smoking-free days.

spans.text: We used the flexible factorial design implemented within SPM5 ( http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm ) to obtain the main effect of groups (NS, SQ, and UQ).

model_settings.value: Flexible factorial design in SPM5; analyses adjusted for age, gender, years of education, risky alcohol use, pulmonary disease, geriatric depression scale score, and gray- and white-matter partitions.

spans.text: The analyses were adjusted for age, gender, years of education, risky alcohol use, pulmonary disease, geriatric depression scale score and the amount of gray and white matter partitions.

footer.value: *Refers to comparisons between never smokers who were available for follow up (In) and those who were not (Out). caption.value: Baseline characteristics of never smokers, successful and unsuccessful quitters.

footer.value: NS = never smoker; SQ = successful quitter; UQ = unsuccessful quitter. These participants completed 24 months of follow up. p-value: probability that the observed differences between the three groups may have arisen by chance, as determined by one way analysis of variance for count variables (e.g., ADAS-cog score) and Pearson's chi-square for categorical variables (e.g., presence of cardiovascular disease). SD = standard deviation; IQR = interquartile range. *p ≤ 0.01, difference between NS and SQ arising from t-tests for count variables and Pearson's chi-square for categorical variables. # p ≤ 0.01, difference between NS and UQ arising from t-tests for count variables and Pearson's chi-square for categorical variables. There were no significant differences between participants in the SQ and UQ groups.
